شَرِيبٌ : see شَرَابٌ: and شَرُوبٌ; the latter in five places. ＝
-A2- Also One who drinks with another: (S, K:) and one who waters his camels with those of another: of the measure فَعِيلٌ in the sense of the measure مُفَاعِلٌ: (S:) and one who draws water, or is given to drink, with another. (IAar, K.) You say, هُوَ شَرِيِبِى [He is my companion in drinking; or in watering his camels with mine: &c.]. (TA.) And a rájiz says, “رُبَّ شَرِيبٍ لَكَ ذِى حُسَاسِ
كَالحَزِّ بِالمَوَاسِى ↓ شِرَابُهُ
” [Many a one who waters his camels with thine, or who draws water with thee for the watering of camels, having an evil disposition, his watering &c. is like the cutting with razors]: i. e., thy waiting for him at the watering-trough is [a cause of] killing to thee and to thy camels. (TA.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
